name: rock
summary: Weathered stone in the open: a boulder, a wall, a tomb. Cracked, lichened, never cut smooth.
why: Metallic 0.0. Stone is a dielectric and the mistake to avoid is the one wood had - a
metallic rock is a lump of pewter with a granite decal on it.
Roughness 0.86, the highest in the library and higher than skin's 0.78. Nothing on a
weathered boulder is polished. The one thing that could argue lower is wet stone, which
Lorencia has by the well and the waterspout, and that is a different material rather
than a lower figure on this one.
The grain is cast, not brushed. Rock has no direction: it is broken along whatever
planes it broke along, and a brushed normal would lay parallel scratches down a boulder
and make it look turned on a lathe. Cast is the same argument that put it on plate_steel
and the axe's collar, applied to the surface that most obviously has no grain to it.
Scale 210 and depth 0.30. Much the deepest normal here - brass is 0.14 and steel 0.010 -
because on stone the relief is the surface. MU's rock art is already drawing cracks and
pits as colour, and unlike a woodgrain those really do sit millimetres proud and deep,
so the normal has something true to add rather than something to invent.
Roughness range 0.10: a boulder's hollows hold dust and its high points get rained on,
so it varies, but not the way a worn metal edge does.
